Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in manufacturing. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

ERP and accounting

System of record for items, price lists, sales and purchase orders, inventory, invoices and receivables. We read through APIs or scheduled exports and write back only approved drafts or status fields.

  • Tally Prime
  • SAP Business One
  • SAP S/4HANA
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central
  • Oracle NetSuite
  • Odoo or ERPNext

B2B marketplaces and enquiry channels

Sources of new enquiries and RFQs. We connect through official APIs, exports or notifications and route each lead into the CRM with its source recorded.

  • IndiaMART Lead Manager
  • TradeIndia
  • ExportersIndia
  • Website RFQ forms
  • Shared RFQ mailbox

Channel sales and dealer tools

Hold dealer masters, territories, visits, secondary sales and opportunities. Automations use them to route enquiries, plan beats and show dealers their own orders and ledgers.

  • Distributor management system (DMS)
  • Sales force automation apps such as Bizom
  • Dealer and customer portals
  • CRM account and opportunity records

Shop floor and maintenance

Provide production, downtime, rejection and maintenance data. We read and model this data for reporting and reminders; machine control stays entirely within plant systems.

  • MES or shop-floor data collection
  • SCADA, DCS or PLC historian exports
  • CMMS such as SAP PM or IBM Maximo
  • Shift logbooks in Excel or Google Sheets

Quality and laboratory systems

Records of quality events, tests and releases. In GxP environments they remain the validated record; automations read status only and never edit or sign records.

  • QMS such as TrackWise, MasterControl or Veeva Vault
  • LIMS such as LabWare or STARLIMS
  • Calibration and equipment logbooks
  • NCR and complaint registers

GST, logistics and export systems

Generate and hold statutory and shipment documents. Workflows read IRN, e-way bill, transporter and export document status to inform buyers and alert dispatch; filings stay with authorized users.

  • E-invoice IRP via ERP or GSP
  • E-way bill system via ERP or GSP
  • Transporter and courier tracking
  • CHA and freight forwarder updates
  • DGFT certificate of origin platform

Engineering and product data

Hold released drawings, revisions and BOMs. Quotes, NCRs and service tickets reference the released revision so everyone works from the same version.

  • SolidWorks PDM
  • Autodesk Vault
  • Siemens Teamcenter
  • Specification sheets and BOM files

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

Enquiry first-response time

Median time from an enquiry arriving in any channel to the first meaningful human response, measured in business hours.

Why it matters: B2B buyers often send the same RFQ to several suppliers; a quick, informed first question keeps you in contention.

Quote turnaround time

Median time from an enquiry being marked qualified to the approved quote being sent, by product family.

Why it matters: Shows whether estimation capacity, missing information or approvals are slowing the sales cycle.

Quote-to-order conversion

Share of quotes sent in a period that become purchase orders, tracked by product, source and region.

Why it matters: Separates enquiry volume from enquiries worth pursuing and shows where pricing or response speed loses deals.

On-time-in-full dispatch

Share of order lines dispatched complete by the date promised to the customer or dealer.

Why it matters: The measure buyers and dealers notice most; it links planning, procurement, production and dispatch.

Overdue receivables share

Value of receivables past their due date divided by total receivables, by dealer, region and aging bucket.

Why it matters: Shows whether credit limits and reminders are working and where working capital is tied up.

OEE where machine data allows

Availability multiplied by performance multiplied by quality for a line or machine, using agreed planned time, standard rates and good-output definitions.

Why it matters: Points improvement effort at the largest losses, provided the definitions are agreed and the source data is trustworthy.

NCR closure time

Median days from a non-conformance being raised to its CAPA being verified as effective.

Why it matters: Slow closure lets defects repeat and weakens your position in OEM and brand-owner audits.

Planned maintenance compliance

Share of preventive maintenance work orders completed within their scheduled window.

Why it matters: Skipped maintenance shows up later as breakdowns, quality drift and safety risk.

Batch completion to release time

Median time from batch completion to the QA release decision, with the waiting time attributed to each pending item.

Why it matters: Finished stock in quarantine ties up working capital; the pending-item breakdown shows which review step needs capacity.

Service resolution against SLA

Share of service and warranty tickets resolved within the contracted or promised time.

Why it matters: Drives AMC renewals and spare-part revenue, and decides whether dealers recommend your products.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
